prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: []
1: ["Preview Your Desktop Companion", "See how your pet will look and react on your desktop screen before finalizing.", "Continue Customizing"]
2: ["Official Adoption Certificate", "Give your companion a name and confirm their new place on your desktop.", "Companion Name", "Official Desktop Citizen"]
3: ["Preparing Desktop Visibility", "Complete these quick steps to ensure your pet displays and responds on screen.", "Verify desktop overlay permission", "Test pet quick-action shortcut key", "Welcome Home!", "Your pet is live on your screen. Right click them anytime for quick options."]
4: ["Tip: Right-click your desktop pet anytime to open control options and settings."]
5: ["Signing in connects your pet's memory to your account so you never lose your companion when logging in again."]
6: ["Preparing Your Pet in Background", "Feel free to minimize this window. We will send a desktop notification when your companion is ready."]
7: ["Select Your Adoption Journey", "Choose whether to pick a pre-made pet companion or craft a custom one from your photos.", "Instant 1-Click Pet", "Custom Photo Companion"]
8: ["Upload Clear Companion Photos", "Use well-lit, front-facing photos of a single pet for accurate 3D model generation.", "High-contrast JPG or PNG files work best. Avoid dark or blurry images."]
9: ["Meet Your Virtual Desktop Companion", "Scroll down to see how your desktop pet interacts, plays, and stays on your screen."]
